drafts.title: AI help for a busy week
drafts.body: Try AI for the family chore list: ask for a simple weekly plan split into 10-minute jobs. Leave out names, addresses and private details. Read it over together and keep what fits. A useful starting point beats another blank page.
bullets: A suggested planning exercise, not a claim of guaranteed results. Human review remains part of the task. No personal anecdote is implied.

drafts.title: Can charging fit your routine?
drafts.body: Before choosing an EV, start with your daily miles and where you can charge. DOE says many drivers can meet daily needs with overnight Level 1 charging. Check your parking, outlet and vehicle requirements first. The best setup is the one that fits family life.
bullets: DOE says many owners can meet daily driving needs overnight with Level 1 on a dedicated branch circuit near parking. Suitability depends on daily mileage, vehicle and electrical capacity.

drafts.title: Check the clock before charging
drafts.body: Does your utility charge less at certain hours? Check before scheduling EV charging. Some utilities offer time-of-use rates. Compare the whole household bill, not just the car: a cheaper overnight rate may come with pricier hours when the family is home.
bullets: DOE confirms some utilities offer residential time-of-use rates. This is a suggestion to compare local tariff terms, not a promised saving.
